subject: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up and next steps

Hi Emma — great to connect earlier. Quick recap from our discovery + the follow-ups we need to size Dedicated capacity for Nimble: 

Recap of needs:
- Primary goal: low-latency, high-consistency inference for patient-facing assistant and clinician summarization pipelines.
- Data sensitivity: some PHI will be processed; you mentioned you're evaluating Private vs Dedicated in a VPC-first setup.
- Current usage (ballpark from call): base ~60 TPS, typical bursts to ~150 TPS; concurrency around 10-12 active sessions.

Sizing clarification questions (to confirm):
1) TPS targets: can you confirm steady-state TPS vs peak burst TPS (we heard ~60 steady, 150 peak; confirm)?
2) Concurrency: is 10-12 concurrent requests a hard target or a goal under heavy load?
3) Token mix: can you confirm average prompt/completion lengths and percent of requests that are long-context (e.g., >1k tokens)?
4) Deployment preference: you said Dedicated with VPC peering looks promising — is Private (customer-managed control plane/on-prem) required for PHI, or is VPC/Dedicated acceptable with your legal team?
5) Preferred GPU family: do you have a preference (H100 vs A100) given cost vs perf tradeoffs?
6) Any hard latency SLOs (p50/p95) we should engineer for?

I've attached a quick capacity calc (redwood_dedicated_capacity_calc.xlsx) with two draft configs: H100-based and A100-based, with conservative autoscaling headroom. If you can answer 1-4 above and share a short traffic sample (per-minute TPS for a week or representative day), we can produce a firm sizing recommendation + cost estimate.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the bullets above and share the CSV traffic sample (nimble_traffic_sample.csv is a template attached).
- I'll loop in Marissa (solutions lead) and Connor (infra) to prep an ops-level sizing.
- We can schedule a 30-min follow-up to review the sizing and procurement path.

Proposed times (PDT): Mon 4/5 10:00-11:30, Tue 4/6 09:00-11:00 — tell me what works and I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scoped.

Best,

From: Emma Li <emma@nimblehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up and next steps

Thanks Aditya — really helpful recap. Answers inline below.

> 1) TPS targets: can you confirm steady-state TPS vs peak burst TPS?
We expect ~60 TPS as a day-to-day baseline for our patient assistant (evening peaks at 80), and larger model-triggered workflows can spike to ~150 TPS for short periods (1-5 minutes) during batch processing windows. For planning, assume steady 60 TPS, occasional bursts up to 150 TPS.

> 2) Concurrency: is 10-12 concurrent requests a hard target?
12 concurrent is a safe target for session-level concurrency; some background summarization jobs add another ~6 concurrent jobs during batch windows. So plan for 18 concurrent in worst-case mixed load.

> 3) Token mix: confirm avg prompt/completion lengths and percent long-context (>1k tokens)?
Average prompt: ~500 tokens; average completion: ~120 tokens. About 25% of requests include long contexts (1k-3k tokens) — those are mainly clinician notes summarization. Also ~10% of traffic is embeddings for search and similarity.

> 4) Deployment preference: Dedicated with VPC peering is preferred initially. We prefer Redwood Dedicated with dedicated GPUs and VPC peering; Private/on-prem is a longer-term option if our legal team requires on-prem for PHI, but that's not a blocker today.

> 5) Preferred GPU family: H100 vs A100?
If price allows, we'd prefer H100 for the latency-sensitive models (smaller response windows and faster context handling), but A100 is acceptable if cost is a constraint. Please show both configs.

> 6) Latency SLOs?
Target p50 < 200ms for short-turn prompts (<= 512 tokens), p95 < 600ms. For long-context jobs we can accept higher p95 (up to 2s) if it reduces cost.

I'll attach a day-of-week sample dump for last week (minimal PII removed) — sending on Monday. Procurement is looped (procurement@nimblehealth.com) for pricing once we have a draft config.

Cheers,
Emma
Emma Li
Principal Product Manager, NLP | Nimble Health
emma@nimblehealth.com

Emma — thanks for the fast turnaround and the detailed answers. We've reviewed and sketched a preliminary dedicated config based on your inputs; attached is an updated sizing workbook with two recommended deployments and rough cost estimates:

Option A — H100-optimized (recommended for latency-sensitive workloads):
- Config: 4x H100 (80GB) nodes in Dedicated pool + 1 warm spare (autoscale policy for bursts).
- Expected steady throughput: ~65-80 TPS with p50 <150ms for <=512 token prompts; headroom for 150 TPS bursts with autoscale to 6 nodes.
- Concurrency: supports ~18 concurrent mixed requests with native KV/prefix caching.
- Notes: better performance on long-context and can reduce per-token cost for heavy-context workloads.

Option B — A100-optimized (cost-conscious):
- Config: 6x A100 (80GB) nodes in Dedicated pool + 1 warm spare.
- Expected steady throughput: ~60-70 TPS; bursts to 150 TPS achievable with autoscale but slightly higher p95 latency (~500-800ms) on tails for long-context requests.
- Concurrency: ~15-18 mixed concurrency depending on batching configuration.

Autoscaling & policies:
- Autoscale triggered on sustained 60s average CPU/GPU utilization and queue depth; immediate burst policy for short spikes (1-5 minutes) to allow inflight batch expansion.
- Recommend prefix/KV caching for clinician templates and session histories to reduce token processing for repeated contexts.

Procurement/next steps:
- I'll provision a demo Dedicated config in our staging infra for validation (no PHI) so you can run a smoke test.
- Marissa can run a more detailed ops sizing based on the sample CSV when you send it.
- If you want, we can prepare an initial SOW + pricing quote for both options to share with procurement - I can have a draft to your procurement contact by EOD Wed 4/7.

Can we do a 30-min ops call to walk through the sizing on Wed 4/7 at 10:00 PDT? Marissa and Connor will join. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda: 1) confirm burst/averaging windows, 2) review autoscale policy, 3) procurement timeline.

DocuSign/pricing: I'll include a draft pricing deck and the SOW link in the calendar invite for procurement review.

Thanks — I'll follow up once I get your sample CSV.
